title: What do the answers share when we change the signs?
description: Plus and minus signs are placed between three, four, five and six in every possible way, and all the signed sums are worked out one by one. The eight answers are listed together on the board and checked for a common feature. Keeko raises the doubt that three gaps and two signs make only six ways.
teaching_notes: One idea: each of the three gaps has its own two choices, so the choices multiply to eight, and every answer turns out to have the same parity. Watch for students who add or mix the choices instead of multiplying them.

source: List all eight signed expressions for 3, 4, 5 and 6 and eval
video_script.why: A learner lists every signed expression systematically, works out each, and sees that all the answers are even.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers: three, four, five and six
video_script.anchor: the four cards three, four, five and six in a row with sign cards in the three gaps, as in the book
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the three gaps by the two signs and gets six instead of multiplying two choices three times
video_script.payoff_line: There are eight expressions, and every answer is even.

final_answer.spoken: eight expressions, and every answer is even

maths_rules: 18, 6, 8, -4, 10, -2, 0 and -12 are all even; even numbers have 2 as a factor, and so do negative even numbers
video_script.design: One idea: list by branching choices, work out all eight, look at the list together. Assumes plus and minus signs on integers. Wrong idea: gaps times signs makes six. The four cards stay fixed and only the sign cards flip.

beats.on_screen: title card Signs Between Numbers; four cards 3, 4, 5, 6 in a row with three empty gaps between them

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the four cards 3, 4, 5, 6 line up
marks.signs: plus and minus cards hover over the three gaps
marks.ask: a question mark glows over the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about four numbers in a row, three, four, five and six.
<bookmark mark='signs'/>Put plus or minus signs between them, in every possible way.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Then work out each answer. What do the answers have in common?

beats.on_screen: the row of four cards stays on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a number line with 18, 6, -4 marked; the words odd and even sit under it; 2 and -2 are marked even

marks.parity: the words odd and even appear as one label named parity
marks.factor: the cards two, minus two and minus four light up as even

narration: <bookmark mark='parity'/>Whether a number is odd or even is called its parity.
<bookmark mark='factor'/>Even numbers have two as a factor, and so do negative ones like minus two and minus four.

beats.on_screen: Given: the numbers 3, 4, 5, 6 in a row, with + or − in each of the three gaps

marks.given: the four numbers and the three gaps are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers are three, four, five and six. Each of the three gaps has plus or minus.

beats.on_screen: To find: all the expressions, the value of each, and what they share
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to list every expression, work out each one, and see what they share.

beats.on_screen: gap 1: 2 choices; gap 2: 2 choices; gap 3: 2 choices. 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 expressions, drawn as a tree

marks.gaps: a tree opens with two branches at each gap
marks.count: the product two times two times two is written under the tree

narration: <bookmark mark='gaps'/>Step one, count the expressions. Every gap has two choices, plus or minus.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Two times two times two gives eight expressions.

marks.first: the first two lines are worked out
marks.second: the next two lines are worked out

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, keep plus four. Three plus four plus five plus six is eighteen. Three plus four plus five minus six is six.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Three plus four minus five plus six is eight. Three plus four minus five minus six is minus four.

marks.first: the first two lines are worked out
marks.second: the next two lines are worked out

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, switch to minus four. Three minus four plus five plus six is ten. Three minus four plus five minus six is minus two.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Three minus four minus five plus six is zero. Three minus four minus five minus six is minus twelve.

beats.on_screen: 18, 6, 8, −4, 10, −2, 0, −12 side by side, each with a factor 2

marks.list: the eight answers slide into one row
marks.even: each answer is tagged with the factor two

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step four, put the answers together: eighteen, six, eight, minus four, ten, minus two, zero and minus twelve.
<bookmark mark='even'/>Each one has two as a factor, so each one is even.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>There are eight expressions, and every answer is even.
All eight have the same parity.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the row of cards
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 3 gaps × 2 signs = 6, struck through; the tree shows 2, then 4, then 8 branches

marks.doubt: the bubble with three gaps times two signs appears
marks.tree: the tree grows from two to four to eight branches
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and eight is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks there are six ways, because three gaps with two signs make three times two.
<bookmark mark='tree'/>But every gap splits each branch in two again. The branches grow from two to four to eight.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The choices multiply, so there are eight ways, not six.
